The volume title page at line 2819 reads POEMS by EMILY DICKINSON, Second Series, Edited by two of her friends MABEL LOOMIS TODD and T.W. HIGGINSON; the preface closes AMHERST, MASSACHUSETTS, August, 1891; the epigraph beginning My nosegays are for captives follows; then the heading I. LIFE. and the numeral I.; then the poem, untitled, whose first two lines read I'm nobody! Who are you? and Are you nobody, too? That is the proposed wording character for character, with the lower case nobody the 1891 editors imposed. Lineation, capitals at the line head, and the closing question mark are the edition's own, and the slash preserves the edition's two lines. Locator Poems, Second Series, Life I, lines 1 to 2 is right: Life is part I of the Second Series and this is poem I within it. Fame: the opening line of one of the best known poems in English. TWO NOTE FIXES, neither of them a refutation. First, the note says the manuscript reads Are you, Nobody, too, but the manuscript and the Johnson and Franklin texts print dashes, Are you, dash, Nobody, dash, too, not commas; as written the note invents a third reading that exists nowhere, which is the one thing this track forbids. Rewrite as: the 1891 editors regularised the manuscript's capitals and dashes, so the card names the edition whose wording it uses. Second, the source line gives a title in single quotes while the note says the poem is untitled in this edition; first line as title is the standard Dickinson convention, but the note should say so rather than appear to contradict the source.
